argument:
IHH's adjusted operating growth supports real hospital expansion, but cash conversion leaves a thin shareholder cushion: H1 surplus after specified financing and leases was RM141m against RM486m owner dividends. Net debt of RM11.564bn before RM2.205bn leases adds sensitivity to funding costs and future capex at a 30.38x trailing multiple.

The bull's RM771m pre-financing FCF is a useful cash anchor, but subtracting obligations changes payout capacity materially. Faster EBITDA than revenue growth can support future coverage, not establish it now. Singapore admissions weakness and unresolved governance disclosures remain relevant without presuming adverse legal outcomes. A growth purchase may be defensible, but dividend restraint and improved conversion are concrete conditions for compensation; the weak chart does not itself invalidate operating progress.
key_points: Post-financing cash falls short of dividends.
Net debt and leases increase conversion sensitivity.
Underlying growth does not erase funding and governance risks.
rebuttal_to_previous: The bull's pre-financing FCF overstates available payout capacity if used alone: RM141m remained after specified obligations versus RM486m dividends. Strong adjusted growth must improve this thin coverage to justify the premium.
